articles.title: Newly Discovered Species of Jellyfish Found in Mediterranean Sea
articles.summary: Researchers at the University of Alicante have identified a previously unknown species of jellyfish in the waters off the coast of Alicante.
articles.content: Researchers in Spain have unearthed a previously unknown species of jellyfish lurking in the waters off the coast of Alicante. This latest find adds to the growing list of mysterious creatures discovered in the Mediterranean Sea, which is often considered one of the most thoroughly studied bodies of water on the planet. The newly identified species, Copula lucentia, measures only a few millimeters in diameter and has been found to be the second box jellyfish species documented in the Mediterranean. This classification comes after Carybdea marsupialis was described by Swedish botanist Carl Linnaeus back in 1758. Researchers at the University of Alicante's Marine Laboratory collected specimens of Copula lucentia between 2016 and 2018, measuring them to be anywhere from 1 to 7 millimeters in size. In order to formally describe the species, researchers combined morphological studies with genetic analyses conducted in collaboration with international specialists. According to Dr. Eva Fonfría, lead author of the study and a researcher at the University of Alicante, the discovery was made during a sampling campaign. Initially, researchers were surprised by the jellyfish's small size for that time of year, and its unique morphological features didn't quite fit with what they had expected. Researchers used genetic analyses to confirm the identity of Copula lucentia as a distinct species. The study, published in 2024 in the journal Marine Biodiversity, represents an important step forward in understanding the biodiversity of the Mediterranean Sea. The team of scientists behind the discovery analyzed the jellyfish specimens and compared them with known species, which revealed distinctive features that warranted classification as a new species. Further investigation confirmed that the organism belonged to the genus Copula but exhibited characteristics that set it apart from other members of this group. A Latin name has been assigned to the newly discovered species: Copula lucentia. This designation pays tribute to Lucentum, the ancient Roman name for Alicante, where the specimens were found. The region off El Campello on the Alicante coastline is now recognized as a significant site for further research into this new species and its behavior in its natural habitat. The discovery of a new jellyfish species in the waters off Alicante in Spain has significant implications for marine research. According to César Bordehore, senior lecturer in the Department of Ecology at the University of Alicante, this finding marks a major milestone in the field. Bordehore emphasizes that there is still much to be learned about the biodiversity of the Mediterranean Sea. The identification of a second box jellyfish species highlights the need for continued research into the region's marine ecosystems. Despite the importance of this discovery, many questions remain unanswered about the new jellyfish. Its reproductive cycle, its role in the food web, and its ability to sting are all areas that require further investigation. The presence of small marine organisms such as salps, tintinnids, and jellyfish can have a significant impact on key areas like fisheries. These tiny creatures prey on fish eggs and larvae, which is crucial for understanding their role in maintaining the balance of marine ecosystems. As part of an ongoing effort to restore fish stocks in the Mediterranean while protecting vulnerable species, a team led by Bordehore is working on the Sea4Future project. This Horizon Europe initiative brings together partners from 12 countries to study interactions with gelatinous organisms and promote sustainable fishing practices. The Oceanogràfic is playing a key role in this collaborative effort, providing expertise in marine fauna recovery and public awareness of the importance of protecting and restoring marine ecosystems. By working together, researchers aim to gain a better understanding of the complex relationships within these ecosystems. The sampling campaign organized with the Oceanogràfic in Valencia has yielded a significant haul of specimens from the newly discovered jellyfish species. Over 200 individuals have been collected for further study, providing researchers with valuable material to analyze and understand this previously unknown species. Some of these animals are being kept and displayed in the Medusa Lab at the Oceanogràfic, where scientists are working to help them grow and explore whether their life cycle can be completed under controlled conditions. Biologists are particularly interested in bringing the specimens to sexual maturity so that they can reproduce, a challenging task given that this is the first time this species has been kept in an aquarium. As part of the ongoing research, experts from the University of Alicante's marine ecology department are collaborating with Oceanogràfic staff to gain insights into the jellyfish's biological requirements. The discovery of a new jellyfish species off the coast of Alicante in Spain has significant implications for our understanding of marine biodiversity. The research team is working to identify the biological requirements that allow this species to thrive in its specific environment. This effort involves analyzing data on water temperature, salinity, and other factors that may influence the jellyfish's behavior and survival. By gaining insights into these conditions, scientists can better understand how to protect and conserve marine ecosystems worldwide. This research will contribute to a broader understanding of the complex relationships between species and their environments. articles.title: Women's Temperature Sensitivity Linked to Testosterone Levels
articles.summary: Research suggests that women feel chilly more easily than men due to differences in skin sensor activation triggered by testosterone levels.
articles.content: Women often feel chilly more easily than men, a common observation that has been noted across various species, including humans. Research conducted on mice suggests that this difference in temperature sensitivity may be linked to testosterone levels. The study found that the skin sensors responsible for detecting heat and cold are activated at higher temperatures in female mice compared to their male counterparts. This subtle distinction results in a noticeable shift in preferred temperature, with females preferring warmer environments by roughly 7 degrees Fahrenheit (4 degrees Celsius) more than males. Scientists believe that testosterone plays a role in this difference, influencing the activation of these skin sensors. According to study co-author Peter McNaughton, a pharmacologist at King's College London, while this observation may seem innocuous, it has significant practical implications for designing spaces and buildings that accommodate people's varying temperature preferences. The study's findings suggest that female mice are more sensitive to cold temperatures than male mice. This is not a unique phenomenon, as it has been observed in other female animals, including birds. The researchers set out to investigate this difference by creating an experiment where mice were given the choice between two plates with different temperature settings. In one plate, the temperature was kept at 4 degrees Fahrenheit (33 degrees Celsius), while the second plate varied between lower and higher temperatures. A camera tracked the mice's movements, calculating how much time they spent on each plate. Interestingly, when the first plate was warmer than the second, female mice still preferred to stay on the warmer plate. When the temperature difference between the two plates increased, female mice showed a more pronounced preference for the warmer plate. In one instance, where the second plate was 4 degrees Fahrenheit (38 degrees Celsius) cooler than the first, female mice spent significantly more time on the warmer plate than male mice did. This trend continued even when the temperature difference was smaller. The researchers are careful to note that the air temperature in the cage did not affect the mice's preferences, as the top of the cage was left open. Therefore, it can be inferred that the female mice's preference for warmth is driven by their skin sensors detecting changes in temperature. Research into the differences between male and female thermoregulation has led scientists to investigate how sex hormones influence temperature sensing in mice. Studies have shown that women tend to feel cold more easily than men, but the underlying reasons for this disparity are not well understood. To shed light on this phenomenon, researchers turned their attention to the genetic factors at play. By examining the role of testosterone in male mice, they aimed to uncover how sex hormones influence temperature perception. The deletion of a protein responsible for detecting warmth resulted in reduced avoidance of warmer surfaces among males, indicating that testosterone plays a crucial role in regulating heat-sensing nerves. This protein, which is also present in females but does not seem to be affected by its absence, sends signals discouraging males from staying on warm surfaces. In contrast, the preferred temperature of male mice rose significantly after this deletion. The findings suggest that sex hormones such as testosterone influence the function of temperature-sensing nerves in the skin, leading to differences in thermoregulation between men and women. This difference is not due to variations in internal or skin temperatures, which were found to be similar across sexes. The study found that when male mice were given a drug to block testosterone production, they began to prefer warmer temperatures more easily than males with normal testosterone levels. In fact, these male mice spent significantly more time on a 38 C plate weeks after the treatment compared to their counterparts without the testosterone-blocking medication. This suggests that testosterone plays a significant role in temperature regulation and perception. The researchers observed no such effect when they gave female mice testosterone, as they lost their preference for warmer temperatures instead. Interestingly, introducing female hormones into male mice did not alter their temperature preferences, nor did blocking hormones in female mice have any impact on their perception of temperature. Research on mice has shed light on why women tend to get cold more easily than men. The study found that warm and cool temperatures are processed by the brain through separate pathways, which may explain why women's sensitivity to cold is heightened. Interestingly, this discovery could have implications for understanding conditions such as neuropathic pain, where people experience an increased sensitivity to temperature extremes. By studying how temperature sensors work in the body, scientists hope to gain a better understanding of these mechanisms and potentially develop new treatments. This research provides valuable insights into the complex process of temperature perception, suggesting that the same sensor proteins found in mice are also present in humans, and likely function in a similar way. articles.title: Paraguayan lawmakers remove President Santiago Peña over Ueno Bank collapse
articles.summary: Prosecutors have taken former President Santiago Peña in for questioning amid an investigation into allegations of breach of trust and other offenses tied to the bank's collapse.
articles.content: Paraguay's former President Santiago Peña has been taken in for questioning by prosecutors at the attorney general’s office just hours after being removed from power by Congress over the collapse of a major bank. The sudden removal and subsequent questioning come as Paraguay's Central Bank works to compensate hundreds of thousands of people who were left unable to access their accounts following the bank's closure. The financial institution, Ueno Bank, had its operations frozen, leaving nearly 3 million customers locked out of their savings. As Peña arrived at the attorney general’s compound, he was seen in drone footage taken by Paraguay's Telefuturo wearing navy blue pants and a white shirt, without being handcuffed. He was escorted to the compound in a black SUV accompanied by police officers. The questioning is part of a wider investigation into allegations of breach of trust and other offenses tied to the bank's collapse, with prosecutors having ordered Peña's arrest along with that of former Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo on Friday. Paraguayan lawmakers have pressed on with impeachment proceedings against former President Mario Abdo Peña after his resignation was rejected by Congress. Following Peña's departure, Vice President Pedro Alliana took over and began assembling a new Cabinet. Meanwhile, the Central Bank announced that 1.2 million Ueno customers had received reimbursement of their insured deposits, as mandated by Paraguayan law. Opposition lawmakers have accused Peña of misusing his power to direct public funds into Ueno, while regulators allegedly turned a blind eye to high-risk lending practices involving insiders. The allegations have sparked widespread outrage and calls for accountability. The crisis marks the most significant political upheaval in Paraguay in over a decade, with opposition Sen. Yolanda Paredes urging that Peña be held accountable by being sent to prison rather than allowed to leave office with immunity. Peña's departure from office has sparked a mix of emotions in Paraguay as the country struggles to recover from the bank collapse. His farewell message expressed hope that his exit would prevent further harm to the nation. Public outcry against Peña and Ueno continues to escalate with thousands of protesters clashing with police, demanding access to their frozen savings and accountability for the bank's failure. The largest teachers' union in Paraguay has announced plans to begin an indefinite national strike on Monday to protect public pension funds, adding to the pressure on authorities to take action against those responsible for the collapse. articles.title: Heavy Rainfall Accelerates Glacier Movement in Alaska
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that heavy rainfall can suddenly accelerate glacier movement in Alaska, causing significant damage to surrounding landscapes.
articles.content: Glaciers in Alaska are known for their slow and steady movement down mountainsides, but researchers have discovered that heavy rainfall can suddenly accelerate them, causing significant damage to the surrounding landscape. When glaciers surge, they can move at speeds many times faster than their normal pace, carving out valleys, creating crevasses on their surface, blocking side valleys with temporary lakes behind, or even triggering catastrophic flooding when these ice dams burst. This rapid movement has a profound impact on rising sea levels as glaciers melt and calve into the ocean. Scientists are eager to understand the mechanisms behind glacier surges, particularly in relation to climate change, making it essential for them to monitor the instabilities of world's glaciers. By studying glacier behavior, researchers can gain valuable insights into the complex relationships between glaciers, rain, and sea levels. To investigate how rain affects glacier movement, a team of researchers led by Parker Wilkerson from Boise State University chose to study the Sít' Kusá (Turner Glacier) in Alaska, which is known for its steep terrain and numerous crevasses. The researchers used GPS measurements from instruments around the glacier to track its position every 15 seconds and monitor changes in short-term speeds compared to longer-term movement. These data were paired with rain estimates validated by nearby weather station readings at Yakutat Airport. During a period of surge (2020–2021) versus slow flow (2022–2024), it was found that over half of rainfall events triggered speed-ups, with the highest daily increase reaching 7.5 meters in just one day - more than double the normal rate. The surge also lasted twice as long as any during the quiescent period and typically began about 12 hours after heavy rain started, when precipitation exceeded at least 20 mm. The glacier returned to a stable state three days later. Rain-induced speed-ups were less frequent during periods of slow flow but were more intense when they did occur, requiring 60 mm of rain since the start of the event and resulting in a much bigger percentage increase (251%) in speed. These speed increases were proportionately larger given the glacier's slow background movement, even though they only peaked at an average of 1.5 meters per day - still more than double the normal rate. Glacier acceleration was not uniform across both phases, with speeds increasing more rapidly in downhill sections compared to areas higher up in the valley. This disparity is thought to be influenced by a combination of factors, including the landscape topography and gravity. The researchers attribute this phenomenon to the efficiency of the glacier's drainage system. An efficient drainage network allows rainwater and meltwater to drain away quickly, enabling the glacier to maintain its steady advance on the underlying bedrock. However, an inefficient drainage system can hinder movement by trapping water in isolated pockets under the ice or in the sediment beneath it. As more water enters these areas, pressure builds up against the weight of the overlying ice, reducing friction and creating a lubricating layer that facilitates rapid sliding over the underlying ground. This process is known as basal sliding, which can also occur when the weight of the ice reaches a critical point, causing high pressure to alter the temperature at which it melts. The relationship between drainage efficiency and glacier speeds is crucial for scientists to refine their model projections of ice loss into the future. With shifting weather patterns leading to more frequent heavy rain events, glaciologists are likely to see an increase in surges in years to come. These surges can have devastating consequences for coastal and island communities, particularly those at risk of flooding due to rising sea levels. The increased melting of glaciers in a warmer world will only exacerbate this problem, making it essential for scientists to understand the implications of glacier ice loss. Glacier drainage systems are complex and dynamic, changing on various timescales from decadal to daily. This makes it challenging for scientists to predict how glaciers may behave in a warmer world, as some components of their behavior remain inherently unpredictable. The ever-changing nature of glaciers means that models must be continually refined to account for new data and observations. As researchers strive to better understand the relationship between drainage efficiency and glacier speeds, they will need to incorporate emerging findings into their projections of ice loss. Heavy rain can have a significant impact on glacier speeds in Alaska, with new research suggesting that it can more than double these rates. The study found that during intense rainfall events, glaciers in Alaska's temperate regions experience rapid acceleration, which can lead to increased ice loss and potentially catastrophic consequences for the surrounding environment. This phenomenon is attributed to the increased drainage efficiency of the glacier due to heavy rain, allowing meltwater to flow more freely through the ice. articles.title: AI Chatbots Becoming Major News Sources for Millions
articles.summary: Millions of people are increasingly turning to AI chatbots as a source of news, seeking quick answers to questions about current events.
articles.content: Millions of people are increasingly turning to AI chatbots as a source of news, seeking quick answers to questions about current events. According to a 2026 survey by the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, over 10% of the global population uses AI chatbots for news on a weekly basis. This trend is particularly pronounced among younger audiences, who are more likely to rely on these tools for information. The rise of AI-powered news sources has significant implications for the traditional role of journalism. For decades, media organizations have sent reporters into the field and conducted research to produce stories that explain complex global events to their audiences. As people increasingly turn to AI chatbots for news, the relationship between those producing journalism and those distributing it is changing. Traditionally, search engines like Google would direct users to reputable news sources in exchange for traffic and advertising revenue. Julia Becker, publisher of Funke Media Group, noted at a recent panel discussion that the old model of search engines directing users to quality reporting has broken down. The issue of copyright infringement has become a pressing concern in the media industry as publicly available news is increasingly being copied and summarized by artificial intelligence chatbots. As a result, news organizations are finding it harder to rely on the revenue generated from distributing their work, which was once a key source of income. This shift has sparked a growing debate about who should benefit financially from the use of copyrighted material in AI systems. Media houses are now pushing "Big Tech companies to obtain permission before using their content and to compensate them for it. In Germany, several major players in the industry have joined forces to advocate for stronger copyright protections. In the US, lawsuits against companies accused of infringing on copyrights are adding pressure. The New York Times has taken internet firm Brave Softwar to court over allegations that it used the newspaper's content without permission and bypassed its paywall. The European Union is also examining the issue, with legal institutions such as the European Court of Justice considering whether AI-generated answers can themselves infringe on copyright laws. The use of journalistic content by AI companies has sparked concerns about compensation for publishers and journalists. Their work becomes part of the answers generated by these systems, raising questions about ownership and payment. AI companies should not only utilize high-quality journalism but also compensate its creators, according to experts. This view emphasizes the need for a fair financial arrangement between AI developers and the media industry. Two primary ways AI companies employ journalistic material have been identified: training their models and generating responses to user queries in real time. The latter is considered an urgent issue, as it involves using journalism directly to answer individual questions. European copyright law may offer a solution to part of this problem, argue experts. Under current EU regulations, publishers and journalists can claim collective payment for the use of their work, potentially without requiring new legislation. A collecting organization could be established to gather payments from AI companies and distribute them fairly among publishers and journalists, much like music royalties are collected and distributed. Publishers and authors may use a standardized rate system as a starting point when negotiating individual licensing deals with AI companies once such a system is established. Google has expressed willingness to negotiate agreements with German media companies and discuss new AI products with them, according to Lutz Mache, the company's senior manager of government affairs and public policy. The tech giant is also testing an AI Contribution" pilot program, which aims to reward content that plays a significant role in answers generated by its AI-powered products like Gemini and AI Overviews. However, this initiative remains in its experimental phase and is not a comprehensive payment system available to all publishers. Several major players in the field have recently endorsed clearer signals for website owners to indicate whether their content can be used to train AI models. Microsoft, Anthropic, and OpenAI are among those advocating for more standardized and transparent approaches to AI usage. Jörg Heidrich, a lawyer specializing in technology law and serving as AI commissioner at Heise, has cautioned against hastily introducing new regulations without considering their broader implications on the tech sector. He argues that Europe's competitiveness could be compromised by excessive regulation, potentially hindering European companies' ability to compete with major global providers. The debate over copyright and payment for news content generated by artificial intelligence (AI) systems may overlook smaller players such as startups, independent developers, and research institutions. These entities rely on access to data to develop and train AI systems, and new restrictions could potentially hinder their work. articles.title: Airbnb's Founding Roots in San Francisco Home
articles.summary: Brian Chesky recalled how his business idea was born out of necessity in his San Francisco home.
articles.content: In a remarkable story of entrepreneurial spirit and adaptability, Brian Chesky, CEO of Airbnb, recalled how his business idea was born out of necessity in his San Francisco home. At the time, he had quit his job and was struggling to pay rent after making a cross-country move. The situation took an unexpected turn when Chesky realized that local hotels were fully booked due to a conference. The turning point came when Chesky opened up his home to guests as a makeshift accommodation, offering three inflatable air beds for a fee. This initial setup laid the foundation for what would eventually become Airbnb's global platform of over 9 million listings worldwide. The business idea was simple yet innovative: providing an alternative to traditional hotels by allowing people to book homes anywhere in the world. Chesky and his cofounder Joe Gebbia were driven by a desire to make money while meeting new friends through their accommodation venture. Their home soon became a hub for guests, and the duo began to see the potential of expanding this concept beyond just their own space. In 2008, they launched Airbnb with Nathan Blecharczyk, who had previously been Gebbia's roommate. Growing up in Albany, New York, Chesky was encouraged by his social-worker parents to pursue a high-paying career. However, he took an unconventional path and enrolled at the prestigious Rhode Island School of Design to study art. Little did they know that their son would eventually turn his passion for design into a revolutionary business idea that would disrupt the hospitality industry forever. Chesky's early career path was far from what his parents had envisioned for him. Despite their encouragement to pursue a high-paying job, he instead opted to attend art school and develop his design skills. This decision would later prove to be a crucial factor in the creation of Airbnb, but it also led to skepticism among potential investors. Chesky and his co-founder Joe faced an uphill battle as they sought to secure funding for their startup. Their design background was seen as a liability by many business veterans who did not take them seriously. This perception would prove to be short-sighted, as the duo's unique approach to hospitality would eventually revolutionize the industry. Chesky has spoken out about the challenges he faced in securing investment, stating that potential investors viewed him and his co-founder solely based on their appearance rather than their business acumen. Airbnb's unconventional approach to marketing caught the attention of Paul Graham, founder of startup accelerator Y Combinator, after designing presidential-candidate-themed cereal boxes. This unusual tactic marked a turning point for the company in securing investment. Chesky has emphasized that creative companies are more likely to innovate and produce groundbreaking ideas, rather than being constrained by short-term measurable outcomes. He believes this approach is essential for driving progress and growth. As Airbnb experienced rapid expansion, it faced new challenges related to scaling its operations. The company was forced to refocus its efforts at various points, adapting to the changing needs of the business. This has been a recurring theme throughout Airbnb's history. The short-term rental market continues to face regulatory hurdles, with cities in Europe and New York implementing restrictions on rentals for less than 30 days or prohibiting tourist apartment licenses altogether. In the US, housing advocates have raised concerns that short-term rentals are essentially becoming hotels, displacing long-term residents. Airbnb has continued to resist regulatory efforts aimed at limiting short-term rentals, arguing that such restrictions would reduce affordable accommodation options for travelers. The company's stance is reflected in its recent policy update, which shifts responsibility from guests to hosts with regards to certain tasks typically performed by cleaners. This change, set to take effect on November 20 for bookings made on or after that date, has sparked a mixed reaction among hosts and customers alike. articles.title: US Cities with Starter Homes Priced Over $1 Million Reach Record High
articles.summary: A record number of US cities now have starter homes priced at over $1 million, leaving first-time buyers struggling to enter the market.
articles.content: A record number of US cities now have starter homes priced at over $1 million, leaving first-time buyers struggling to enter the market. The affordability crisis has taken hold in areas meant for new homeowners, forcing them to delay their purchases even further. According to a recent Zillow report, 242 American cities now feature median home prices exceeding $1 million, up from just 80 before the pandemic and an increase of 226 cities over the past year. This surge is having a profound impact on the traditional demographic of first-time buyers. The typical age of these buyers has risen to a record high of 40 as they delay their purchases due to rising prices. Millennials, in particular, are finding it increasingly difficult to enter the market during their peak household spending years and as they begin forming families. New Jersey and New York have seen significant growth in million-dollar starter homes, adding 15 cities each to the list over the past year alone. The two states now account for more than half of all new additions to the list, with New Jersey jumping from one city to 26 and New York increasing its total to 41. The New York City metro area is leading the charge, boasting an astonishing 63 cities where starter homes exceed $1 million in price. This rapid growth has left many first-time buyers feeling priced out of the market, as they struggle to find affordable options for their new families. The rapid growth of housing prices has not been limited to a single region or market. In fact, six out of the top 10 most competitive housing markets in the country are located in the Northeast, according to Zillow's analysis for 2026. This region has historically struggled with new construction and inventory deficits, exacerbating the affordability crisis. The combination of intense demand and low mortgage rates has driven up home values at an unprecedented pace, making it increasingly difficult for buyers to afford even starter homes. For those in the Northeast, this perfect storm has pushed housing prices to record levels. Typically, first-time homebuyers are younger individuals, but recent data suggests that this demographic is getting older. According to a report released by the National Association of Realtors in November 2025, the average age of first-time buyers has risen to an all-time high of 40. This shift highlights the growing challenges faced by those attempting to enter the housing market. The number of first-time homebuyers has plummeted in recent years, with last July's numbers representing just half of what is considered a historical norm. This decline underscores the severity of the affordability crisis and its impact on the lives of prospective buyers. As starter homes become increasingly unaffordable, the bar for entry into the housing market continues to rise. The prevalence of million-dollar cities has created significant barriers to entry, requiring buyers to secure large down payments and higher incomes just to afford a home. The strain on affordability is particularly pronounced in markets where prices have reached $1 million or more, leaving many prospective buyers struggling to make ends meet. As one industry expert noted, the situation has worsened over the past couple of years, with no signs of improvement in sight. The affordability crisis gripping the US housing market is now affecting regions that were previously immune to it. According to Zillow's definition of a starter home as one in the lowest third of home values in a given region, over 200 cities have seen prices skyrocket, with some reaching as high as $1 million. This phenomenon is being driven by the lingering effects of the pandemic housing boom, which has pushed up prices nationwide. In fact, the typical starter home value across the country rose 1.7% to $198,649 in June, a relatively modest increase compared to the massive price jumps seen in some regions. The list of cities with $1 million starter homes is no longer limited to coastal areas alone. Before 2020, only Colorado was a non-coastal state with such high prices. However, the pandemic has now spread this phenomenon to 26 states, up from just nine previously. Some of these states have multiple cities with starter home prices exceeding $1 million. States like Texas, Wyoming, and Illinois are among those that have seen significant increases in starter home prices. California still leads the way with 105 cities, but the Northeast is experiencing the fastest growth. New York and New Jersey added a combined total of 15 new cities to their list over the past year, pushing up their totals to 41 and 26 respectively. The New York City metro area has become a hotspot for unaffordable starter homes, with 63 cities now having prices exceeding $1 million. Other major metros like San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Jose, Miami, and Seattle are also seeing significant price increases, driven by demand and limited supply in these areas. The effects of the pandemic on the housing market have proven to be long-lasting. The combination of a decade-long housing shortage and surging demand, fueled by historically low mortgage rates, has driven up home values at an unprecedented pace. For younger generations, this trend is particularly concerning. Millennials and Gen Z buyers are being edged out of the market by baby boomers who own paid-off homes or have secured cheap pandemic-era mortgages. This has led to a significant delay in major milestones for many Americans. Some individuals are opting for non-traditional solutions to overcome the affordability crisis. Instead of buying their first home, they're choosing to rent long-term or exploring co-living models. This shift is a result of the increasingly unattainable nature of homeownership. The housing market may finally be showing signs of stabilization. With more inventory becoming available and slower price growth, buyers who are financially prepared are in a better position than they were just a year ago. However, it remains to be seen whether this trend will continue. Zillow's research suggests that the typical buyer is now breaking even versus renting after about six years, down from over eight in late 2023. This improvement offers some hope for first-time buyers who are struggling to enter the market. In many parts of the United States, owning a starter home has become an unattainable goal for first-time buyers due to skyrocketing prices. The situation is particularly dire in 242 cities where the median price of starter homes has reached a staggering $1 million. This means that young buyers face significant financial hurdles, including larger down payments and higher monthly mortgage payments. The affordability crisis seems to be affecting areas across the country, but there are some exceptions. According to recent data, Texas appears to be an outlier, with many first-time homebuyers able to achieve their goal of homeownership in this region. articles.title: Ron Schneidermann's demanding schedule as Liftopia CEO had personal costs
articles.summary: Schneidermann reflects on his experience, highlighting the importance of finding balance in professional pursuits during challenging startup periods.
articles.content: CEO Ron Schneidermann has had an extensive career in leading several successful companies, including Liftopia and AllTrails. However, he admits to having learned the hard way about achieving a balance between work and personal life. Schneidermann's experience with Liftopia, a digital marketplace for ski resorts, was particularly grueling. He worked out of a small San Francisco apartment, where he managed to survive on less than $15 per day for an extended period. His diet consisted mainly of canned soup. The sacrifices Schneidermann made during this time were not limited to his financial situation. He also took a significant toll on his personal life. When his first daughter was born four years into Liftopia's development, he only managed to take two days off work. Schneidermann allowed himself just one week for his son's birth three years later, which he considers an improvement at the time but now acknowledges as inadequate. He recalls thinking that sacrificing family time was necessary for the company's success. Despite the demanding schedule and personal costs, Schneidermann's business flourished during this period, eventually generating over $60 million in annual revenue. The grueling pace of startup life often demands sacrifice, but for some entrepreneurs, it can also lead to burnout and a skewed perspective on work-life balance. Schneidermann, who has since re-evaluated his approach, acknowledges that he paid a personal cost during the early days of Liftopia. As he reflects on his experience, Schneidermann highlights the benefits of reframing challenges as opportunities for growth. This mindset shift allowed him to transform perceived weaknesses into strengths. He now views this period with a different lens, one that emphasizes the importance of finding balance in professional pursuits. Schneidermann brought this new perspective to AllTrails when he joined the company in 2015. Two years later, he took on the role of CEO and introduced a unique practice: the first Friday of every month was dedicated to getting employees outside and engaged with nature. This ritual aimed to combat the negative effects of prolonged office work. The lessons learned from his past endeavors have also influenced Schneidermann's approach at Acely, where he now leads as CEO. The company has adopted a monthly "hackathon," where employees take a break from routine tasks to focus on experimenting with AI tools and new ideas in a collaborative environment. A stint at UCLA studying mass communication and business left him working multiple jobs to make ends meet, including a gig at Abercrombie & Fitch that ended in termination three times due to his lack of enthusiasm for the role. After graduating from UCLA in 2000, he took on a job as a business process consultant at Accenture, but this too failed to align with his desired lifestyle. Despite its lucrative salary and association with a Fortune 500 firm, he opted out of this opportunity as well. The experience left him with a profound realization: life is too short to spend it in jobs that don't bring fulfillment. This mindset shift led him away from traditional corporate roles and toward the startup world. He credits his entry into tech to a connection made through mutual acquaintances, which landed him a role at Hotwire, a travel startup later acquired by Expedia. Schneidermann notes that this experience highlights the importance of relationships in securing employment, especially in an increasingly competitive job market where traditional entry points are dwindling. In today's competitive job market, it's not just about having the right skills or credentials, but also about how you approach relationships and networking. Schneidermann highlights the importance of building genuine connections with others in your industry, pointing out that even a small pond can eventually become familiar territory if you stay long enough. This means investing time and effort into cultivating relationships with leaders and peers who can offer valuable guidance and support. According to recent data, many young workers struggle with basic professional norms, with six in 10 bosses admitting they've fired Gen Z employees hired straight out of college due to poor communication, lack of professionalism, and disorganization. This suggests that there's a gap between what employers expect from their employees and the skills and experience that new graduates bring. To succeed, Schneidermann advises young workers to focus on building a reputation through consistent behavior, rather than viewing networking as a transactional activity. He emphasizes the importance of being present and engaged in interactions with others, avoiding ghosting or simply showing up without putting in effort. The CEO's career has been marked by a series of pivots, including his most recent move to Acely, a startup that he had not previously been associated with. The company boasts over 50,000 active users and was used by his high school-aged daughter for SAT prep. Schneidermann's willingness to take on the challenge at Acely was driven by his eagerness to learn the industry, rather than any prior expertise in it. He has successfully navigated multiple career transitions, adapting to new environments with ease. His story serves as a testament to the importance of adaptability and resilience in professional life. articles.content: Thanksgiving dinner is often followed by an assortment of sweet treats, but for some, saving room for dessert isn't enough. A new list of Thanksgiving pie recipes caters to those who want to indulge in a little more. The classic pumpkin pie has always been a staple at Thanksgiving tables, but this year's options take it up a notch with added ingredients like maple syrup and vanilla. Gooey pecan pies and apple pies with double crusts or cinnamon crumble are also making an appearance. But if you're looking for something a bit more adventurous, there are plenty of unique pie recipes to try. Cranberry meringue pies with lime-sharpened curd and butterscotch custard topped with toasted marshmallows offer a twist on traditional flavors. A lattice crust is not just a decorative touch, it's also a testament to the skill of the baker who crafted this pie. Beneath its intricate design lies a filling that combines the sweetness of Honeycrisp apples with the deep flavor of smoky burnt-sugar caramel and the richness of bourbon. To get the most out of this pie, it's essential to let it cool completely before slicing, allowing the flavors to meld together and the filling to set. One reader who has mastered the art of pie-making is a grandmother from Chattanooga, Tennessee, who swears by this recipe as the best she's ever used. Her praise is well-deserved, given the complexity of flavors in this pie. A tangy cranberry-lime curd provides a bold contrast to the sweetness of the meringue topping, creating a delightful balance of tastes and textures. To ensure that the filling sets properly, it's crucial to give the pie plenty of time to cool before serving. The result is a truly show-stopping dessert that's almost too good to eat for breakfast - almost. A pear tart stands out as a compelling alternative to traditional apple pie at Thanksgiving gatherings. To make this dessert, firm-ripe Anjou or Bartlett pears are used in combination with a little nutmeg and a flaky lattice crust. The filling of sweet potato custard is elevated by the addition of fresh ginger and a blend of warming spices such as cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves. A cloud of marshmallow-spiked whipped cream adds an airy texture to the dessert. This vibrant purple pie is inspired by the author's Filipino family traditions, featuring a silky filling made from jarred ube halaya and coconut milk. The pearly marshmallow whip on top adds an extra layer of visual appeal to this striking dessert, making it look almost regal in appearance. In terms of flavor profile, the combination of peanut butter and graham cracker crust evokes the image of a giant peanut butter cup, while the fudgy chocolate layer provides a rich contrast to the airy peanut butter mousse above it. The use of conventional creamy peanut butter is deliberate, as its velvety texture is essential for creating a smooth filling that holds together well. A sweet and indulgent dessert, this pie has all the makings of a decadent treat. A dollop of whipped cream adds a delightful contrast to this sweet and indulgent dessert, elevating the overall experience without overpowering the star of the show, the molasses-infused filling. articles.summary: A family vacation to Switzerland's picturesque Bernese Oberland region had reached a turning point - finding an activity that would captivate the attention of adult children and their partners.
articles.content: A family vacation to Switzerland's picturesque Bernese Oberland region had reached a turning point - finding an activity that would captivate the attention of adult children and their partners. As chief planner, I sought something unconventional to break the ice and create lasting memories. My search led me to Interlaken, where a unique experience caught my eye: floating fondue on Lake Brienz. It was exactly what I had been looking for - an unorthodox yet appealing way to enjoy traditional Swiss cuisine in a breathtaking setting. With over 30 visits to Switzerland under my belt, I've had the privilege of experiencing many of its natural wonders firsthand. From skiing and hiking to whittling my own cow from a block of wood, I'm no stranger to this beautiful country's offerings. As we were about to settle into our accommodations in the Bernese Oberland, I knew that getting everyone excited about family time required something more than just exploring iconic sites like Grindelwald, the Jungfrau, and Eiger mountains. A unique culinary experience was just what we needed to get everyone excited about family time in the Bernese Oberland region of Switzerland. I had heard about a company called Outdoor Switzerland that offered a Cheese Fondue Float experience on Lake Brienz, and I thought this could be the perfect way to win over our group's hearts through their stomachs. The experience had evolved from raclette, which involves scraping toasted cheese onto boiled potatoes, to fondue, Switzerland's national dish, served in ceramic caquelons. Reviews of the tour praised the delicious cheese and wine, as well as the fun atmosphere. The day of the tour turned out to be a perfect September Sunday, with glorious temperatures and bluebird skies, and we were grateful for the leisurely five-minute bus ride from Interlaken's downtown area to the launch site in the small village of Bonigen. The boat glided smoothly onto Lake Brienz, its tranquil surface reflecting the surrounding mountains like a perfect mirror image. The lake's depth is impressive, making it the deepest in the country, and its scenic beauty is undeniable. As we settled into our seats around the tablecloth, Hild began to row us further out onto the lake. The scenery was breathtaking, with towering peaks rising up on either side of us, their reflections creating a sense of symmetry in the still water. The fondue pots were already set up and ready for use, containing a prepared cheese mixture that would soon be bubbling away. I poured it into the heated pots, and the aroma of melting cheese filled the air as it began to warm through. As we waited for the fondue to reach its perfect temperature, my son took charge of the music, playing lively Alpine tunes on the Bluetooth speaker to set a festive mood. A passing cruise boat on Lake Brienz caught sight of our floating fondue party, prompting a friendly exchange of waves and toots from the ship's horn. We enthusiastically returned the greeting, waving at the passengers as they smiled and waved back in response. The warmth of the cheese had finally reached its peak, allowing us to indulge in the pleasure of dipping bread cubes into the melted goodness amidst celebratory toasts for our family adventure. As the fondue pot continued to heat up, it transformed the remaining cheese into "la réligieuse", toasted cheese bits that are typically scraped from the bottom of the pot. The Cheese Fondue Float experience on Lake Brienz in Interlaken is available for booking through Outdoor Switzerland's website, as well as GetYourGuide and Viator. This unique activity can be booked between September and April, weather permitting. Guests should prepare for the colder months by bundling up with coats, beanies, and gloves, as they'll spend up to an hour and a half on the water. Private charters are available for groups of up to eight people, and children over eight years old are welcome to join in on the fun. For those who prefer dessert, Outdoor Switzerland also offers a Swiss Chocolate Fondue experience that pairs perfectly with blankets, hot tea, marshmallows, and fruit dipped into creamy melted chocolate while being rowed along the picturesque Brienzersee. This will be a crucial test for Jonathan Gannon's defense, which has been one of the top-ranked units in the NFL so far this year. The New England Patriots have had an easy ride through some of their schedule, particularly last season when they made it to the Super Bowl. However, their performance in the first half of 2026 raises questions about whether their initial success was due to a favorable draw rather than genuine improvement. Despite scoring six points over their last five games, the Patriots' offense still looks vulnerable against strong defenses like the Packers'. The Patriots' offense has faced a mix of defenses this season, but their performance against top-ranked units has been underwhelming. In four games against defenses ranked eight or better in expected points added (EPA) per play, New England averaged just 15 points. This trend is concerning for the Patriots, especially given the strength of the Packers' defense. Green Bay ranks fifth in EPA per play and has shown its ability to contain high-powered offenses. The team has allowed only 13 points against Dallas and 20 against Detroit in recent weeks. The absence of several key players for the Packers may not be a significant blow, but it's worth noting that tight end Hunter Henry is questionable to play due to injury. His go-to receiver status in recent weeks adds another layer of concern for the Patriots' defense. articles.title: Soil pH Management Requires Long-Term Approach
articles.summary: A recent study from the University of Alberta has highlighted the importance of proactive management of soil pH levels across entire multiyear rotations.
articles.content: Western Canadian farmers are being urged to adopt a long-term approach to managing soil acidity, rather than treating it crop by crop. This shift in strategy is necessary due to the complex interactions between fertilizer use, crop rotation, and corrective lime applications that affect soil pH levels over time. A recent study from the University of Alberta has highlighted the importance of proactive management of soil pH levels across entire multiyear rotations. The research team examined how decades of agricultural practices impact soil acidity and nutrient availability, with a focus on the effects of liming legume forages. The study found that applying lime to legume forages not only promotes their growth but also increases the availability of nitrogen for grain crops in future rotations. This discovery suggests that managing soil acidity is crucial for maintaining productivity across entire rotations, rather than just individual crops. According to Dr. Miles Dyck, a soil scientist and professor at the University of Alberta, "Managing soil acidity is about more than simply maintaining the productivity of individual crops." The research team's findings emphasize the need for farmers to adopt a long-term perspective when managing soil health. The study, published in the Canadian Journal of Plant Science, provides valuable insights into the complex relationships between fertilizer use, crop rotation, and soil acidity. As the researchers note, understanding these interactions is essential for developing effective strategies to maintain soil fertility and ensure future harvests. As farmers in Western Canada continue to adapt to changing agricultural practices, they're facing a growing concern: soil acidity. This issue has historically been less pressing for many prairie farmers, but decades of increased crop diversity, fertilizer applications, and nutrient removal through harvests have made it more significant. Farmers are now noticing the effects of these changes on their yields, often not until soil acidity reaches a level that begins to impact production. Restoring favorable soil conditions at this point can be a time-consuming and costly process. The gradual increase in soil acidity is a result of practices that may seem beneficial, but ultimately contribute to the problem. Soil acidity affects plant growth and crop productivity by altering the availability of essential nutrients and disrupting the activity of beneficial microorganisms. These changes have significant implications for farmers who rely on their land to produce a wide range of crops, including cereals, oilseeds, pulses, and forages. The main prairie crops vary in their sensitivity to soil acidity, with some being more affected than others. If one crop in a rotation is impacted by soil acidity, the subsequent crops will also be negatively affected. This highlights the need for farmers to consider the long-term effects of their practices on soil health. Researchers at a leading university have been studying the impact of synthetic fertilizers and lime on soil health over several decades. The data collected from their research plots reveals that applying crushed limestone powder, or lime, can significantly boost forage yields in legume crops such as alfalfa. The study found that when liming is combined with synthetic fertilizers, it not only increases the absorption of essential nutrients by crops but also enhances biological nitrogen fixation within the alfalfa. This process allows beneficial bacteria associated with the roots of the alfalfa to fix more nitrogen, which can then be utilized by subsequent cereal crops. While wheat and oats were less directly affected by soil acidity, they still benefited from liming in an indirect way. When grown after alfalfa that had been treated with lime, these cereal crops absorbed more nitrogen than usual. This is likely due to the improved growth of the preceding alfalfa crop, which increased the amount of nitrogen fixed by beneficial bacteria. The findings suggest a complex interplay between crops within a rotation and highlight the importance of considering the long-term effects of soil acidity on overall yields. By evaluating the potential benefits of liming for all crops in their rotation, producers can make more informed decisions about how to optimize their agricultural practices. This approach requires a forward-thinking perspective, with producers needing to evaluate the potential benefits of liming over time scales of two or three crop rotation cycles, a period spanning ten to 15 years. Managing soil conditions to benefit one crop can also have long-term effects on subsequent crops. This is evident in prairie farming, where improving growing conditions for a single crop can lead to benefits that become apparent over several years. However, researchers have discovered a surprising contradiction: certain crops, like alfalfa, can actually contribute to soil acidification. As the plant's roots absorb essential nutrients, they release acids into the soil, accelerating pH decline when the crop is harvested and those nutrients are removed from the field. The study highlights how a single crop can improve one aspect of soil fertility while simultaneously contributing to changes in another area. This underscores the need for farmers to carefully consider the effects of their crops on soil acidity when planning rotations and nutrient management. In prairie farming, where rotations often span multiple years, this complexity is particularly relevant. The experiments also showed that synthetic fertilizers can exacerbate soil acidification, even when lime is applied as a corrective measure, suggesting that lime should not be viewed solely as a one-time solution to the problem. The study has revealed that manure is more effective than synthetic fertilizers in slowing down soil acidification, thanks to its ability to replenish essential nutrients like calcium and magnesium in the soil. This helps maintain the soil's capacity to resist changes in pH levels, which is crucial for crop growth. According to Dyck, the findings emphasize the need for long-term consideration of nutrient management strategies. Different types of fertilizers and soil amendments can have significantly different effects on soil chemistry over time. Farmers in Western Canada are increasingly recognizing the importance of regular monitoring and management of soil acidity. This involves testing the soil's pH levels at various depths to identify potential problems before they impact crop productivity. Soil sampling is a critical aspect of managing soil acidity, especially under modern farming practices like zero- or reduced-tillage systems. By testing soil in layers and repeatedly at the same locations over time, farmers can catch acidification issues early on and take corrective action before it's too late. Liming strategies can be employed to protect sensitive crops like alfalfa and pulse legumes from the effects of soil acidity. This involves strategically applying lime to specific areas where soil pH levels are most vulnerable to change. The study highlights that soils are dynamic systems and their responses to management practices can vary over time. This means that farmers need to consider not just the immediate effects of treatments but also how they will influence soil conditions in the long term. Understanding these gradual changes is crucial for maintaining productive agricultural systems, which is essential for future generations. By recognizing the complex interactions between crops, soil, and management practices, prairie farmers can develop more effective strategies to mitigate soil acidity and promote sustainable agriculture. This approach can ultimately help ensure the long-term health of the land. Phys.org : https://phys.org/news/2026-11-soil-acidity-crop-longer-prairie.html

articles.title: Alex Pevtsova's Help Solved My Tiny Home Storage Issues
articles.summary: A local interior designer helped me optimize storage and functionality in my 150-square-foot garage casita.
articles.content: I recently moved into my parents' converted garage, a tiny 150-square-foot casita that was supposed to be temporary. However, making the space feel comfortable and functional proved to be a challenge. The existing bunk bed had to stay for future family visits, but I still needed to make the most of the limited square footage. Seeking professional help seemed like an extravagance when I was trying to save as much as possible after separating from my husband. Nevertheless, I turned to Alex Pevtsova, a local interior designer whose work I admired. Interior design has never been my forte, and I was nervous about sharing photos and a video of the space with her. Despite initial reservations, I sent her pictures and a video of the garage, imagining that she might be horrified by its tiny size and existing furniture. However, Alex's response was surprisingly kind and insightful. She pointed out that the space was already quite functional, which made it easier to identify areas for improvement. Our focus quickly shifted to addressing storage issues in the garage. I needed designated spots for my purse and keys, as well as more shelving for my clothes. Additionally, I required a dedicated area for paperwork and filing, as well as a place to store tools and gift-wrapping supplies that were currently scattered throughout the space. The interior designer's suggestions helped me better understand why my tiny home felt so cluttered and overwhelming. We discussed my needs in more detail, including a dedicated area for paperwork and filing, as well as a place to store tools and gift-wrapping supplies that were scattered throughout the space. To address these requirements, Pevtsova suggested using Ikea's planning software to design a custom wardrobe that would meet my needs. We used this tool to create a plan for a cabinet that could hold clothes and bags, with a shelf around waist height for work papers and organizers. This design allowed me to close the doors and keep the mess out of sight, which was a major consideration given the limited space in my home. The interior designer's guidance helped me make a list of essential items for my tiny home, ensuring that I didn't overspend on things I might not need in the long run. With her expertise, we navigated Amazon's vast selection together, and our collaboration cost $375 at an hourly rate of $150. The total budget for the mini redesign came out to be approximately $768, including my purchases. Buying items with the intention of replacing them a few months later can indeed be costly, as Pevtsova pointed out during our consultation. She played a crucial role in helping me prioritize what I truly needed, thereby saving me time and money. The Amazon route had its drawbacks, however, as the heavy boxes proved difficult for both the delivery driver and myself to transport. The delivery driver struggled to bring them to the porch, and I ended up opening the packages outside before bringing in the wooden pieces one by one due to their weight. The final touches to the interior design have been completed, and the result is a space that feels more functional and peaceful. Removing the awkward hanging cloth shelf made a big difference, allowing for clutter-free storage in the cube unit's bins. The added storage on top of the wardrobe has also opened up the space, giving it a sense of openness. This improvement has been especially welcome during a chaotic time. The designer's input extended to modifying the existing curtains as well, with the removal of grommets allowing for better light blocking when needed. articles.title: Dakota Johnson and Machine Gun Kelly Attend Dinner Together
articles.summary: Dakota Johnson and Machine Gun Kelly were spotted together at a dinner hosted by Khaite in West Hollywood.
articles.content: Dakota Johnson's style has always had a rock-and-roll edge, characterized by effortless hair and strategic flashes of skin beneath layered clothing. As her rumored romance with Machine Gun Kelly gains momentum, Johnson appears to be embracing this aspect of her persona more fully. She was spotted attending a dinner at Dan Tana’s in West Hollywood on Thursday evening, hosted by Khaite, alongside Kelly. For the occasion, Johnson's outfit combined high and low notes: beneath a black zip-up hoodie emblazoned with Death Row Pictures' logo, she wore a Valentino crepe miniskirt featuring delicate lace trimming. Johnson's outfit was elevated by two statement necklaces that added a touch of glamour to her casual look. The first, a tiger's-eye and diamond necklace by Laoli, featured a diamond clasp pendant, while the second, Jessica McCormack's Signature 42-carat Diamond Button Back Necklace, brought an extra dose of sparkle. In contrast, Machine Gun Kelly opted for a bold ensemble that showcased his personal style. He wore an emerald-green satin bomber jacket over a bright yellow hoodie and paired it with loose gray sweatpants, a black beanie, and a red bandana pulled across his face. The couple's shared taste in fashion is not the only area where they align, their approach to relationships seems to be relatively low-key. Despite being spotted together on several occasions since September, including at mutual friend Taylor Swift's New York apartment, they have kept their romance relatively under wraps. Their growing closeness was likely cemented after attending Swift and Travis Kelce's wedding in July, where they were photographed together for the first time. Since then, they have made a handful of public appearances, often in each other's orbit, suggesting that their relationship is gaining momentum. Recent sightings have shown the couple leaving a Los Angeles recording studio together, with Johnson dressed in her signature style of straight-leg jeans and ballet flats under a long leather coat. Their frequent outings suggest they are indeed enjoying each other's company, as evidenced by their appearance at the Chateau Marmont and another dinner date in Calabasas, where both opted for leather jackets. Johnson's affinity for fashion that pushes boundaries is well-known, with Valentino often providing her with a unique blend of romantic femininity and darker undertones. articles.title: US Abrams Tanks Adopt Stealthy Approach in Germany Training Exercise
articles.summary: The 1st Armored Division's Abrams tanks were used in a more stealthy manner during a recent training exercise in Germany, carefully concealed from enemy reconnaissance drones.
articles.content: The US Army's Abrams tanks have been a cornerstone of military power for decades, but at a recent training exercise in Germany, they were taking a new approach to warfare. Instead of charging into battle head-on, the 1st Armored Division's Abrams tanks were being used in a more stealthy manner, with their presence carefully concealed from enemy reconnaissance drones. The Joint Multinational Readiness Center in Hohenfels, Germany was bustling with activity as Army personnel trained for various scenarios, but despite their massive size and heavy armor, the Abrams tanks themselves remained out of sight. They were hidden along treelines and deeper in the forest, using cover to avoid being detected by enemy drones that filled the skies during the exercise. The training environment was designed to mimic the battlefields of Ukraine, where drone proliferation has made it extremely difficult for armored vehicles to move freely without being seen. In this new landscape of overhead surveillance and precision strikes, armored assets have taken heavy losses, raising questions about their continued relevance on modern battlefields. The Ukraine conflict has revealed new vulnerabilities in armored vehicles on the modern battlefield. Tanks and infantry fighting vehicles were once seen as crucial to Ukraine's defense strategy, but their effectiveness has been significantly diminished by the widespread use of drones. In an effort to counter this threat, both sides have equipped their tanks with added protection, such as cage armor. However, this solution is far from foolproof and leaves armored assets exposed to drone attacks. The scale of losses suffered by both Ukraine and Russia underscores the severity of the problem. Multimillion-dollar armored vehicles have been destroyed by drones costing just a few hundred dollars. Drones have transformed the nature of combat, creating a vast "kill zone where soldiers and their vehicles are constantly at risk of being spotted and targeted whenever they move. The expanded danger zone has made large-scale maneuver increasingly difficult across much of the conflict's front line. As the US Army continues to grapple with the evolving nature of modern warfare, a stark reality has emerged: even friendly drones can pose a significant threat on the battlefield. In a recent training exercise, a Ukrainian drone briefly appeared and flew off before it was confirmed as a friendly asset, but its presence served as a sobering reminder that enemy drones could be lurking in the shadows, waiting to strike. The US Army's growing concern about drone threats is not unfounded, with increasing numbers of militaries around the world incorporating unmanned aerial vehicles into their arsenals. This trend has forced NATO allies like the US to reassess their tactics and strategies to counter these emerging threats. In an effort to stay ahead of the curve, the US has been leveraging Ukraine's expertise in countering drone attacks, with Ukrainian soldiers participating in major exercises across Europe alongside American troops. These joint training sessions have provided valuable insights into the vulnerabilities of armored formations on the modern battlefield. During a recent iteration of Combined Resolve, Ukrainian soldiers from the elite 412th Unmanned Systems Brigade, known as Nemesis, successfully challenged US armor, causing roughly 70% of the casualties suffered by an American brigade in the opening two days. The exercise highlighted the need for a fundamental shift in tactics to counter the threat posed by drones. The training area was thoroughly covered by Ukrainian sensing and strike capabilities, rendering even routine practices like clustering vehicles in rear areas to refuel into large targets. This realization has prompted soldiers to rethink long-held assumptions about armored warfare, including the notion that logistics and maintenance can be safely conducted in the open. As armored forces rethink their approach to warfare, decentralized logistics and terrain-aware tactics are emerging as key strategies to avoid being exposed to enemy attacks. In a recent exercise, Combined Resolve, these principles were put to the test, but it became clear that implementation was still a work in progress. For instance, an M1 Abrams tank found itself unable to refuel due to indirect fire, forcing its crew to scatter and eventually leaving the vehicle vulnerable to attack. The incident highlighted the risks of routine operations like refueling when enemy drones and sensors are present, making even mundane tasks hazardous for armored crews. This reality is prompting soldiers to reevaluate their assumptions about logistics and maintenance in open areas. To counter this threat, armor crews are learning new tactics, such as using camouflage nets to conceal their vehicles, adapting their maneuvering techniques, and experimenting with nighttime resupply operations instead of daytime ones. These methods may seem basic, but they represent a fundamental shift in how armored forces operate. In the heat of battle, survival is no longer just about avoiding enemy fire; it's also about minimizing exposure and staying one step ahead of the opposition. Armor crews are recognizing that hiding", even from drone surveillance, is not a guarantee of safety, as revealed during the exercise when the opposing force demonstrated that hiding in a treeline may only provide temporary protection. As the Army continues to grapple with these challenges, it's clear that armored warfare is evolving, and traditional notions about logistics and maintenance are being rewritten. The key to success lies in adapting to this new landscape and developing strategies that prioritize stealth and agility over brute force. The evolving nature of modern warfare demands that armored forces adapt to new challenges on the battlefield. A recent example of successful mechanized maneuver can be seen in Ukraine's Third Army Corps' counteroffensive efforts in the Donetsk region. Ukrainian forces have successfully executed two major assaults behind Russian lines, according to reports from the Third Army Corps. The corps' commander, Gen. Andrii Biletskyi, initially expressed skepticism about the feasibility of such operations but was proven wrong by their success. The Ukrainian armored crews involved in these operations underwent special training and had their vehicles equipped with additional gear to support their mission. This specialized approach allowed them to carry out complex maneuvers on a battlefield dominated by drones and other advanced technologies. Support drones played a crucial role in these operations, operating both as surveillance assets and attack platforms. The use of armored vehicles has become increasingly sophisticated, requiring detailed planning and coordination among multiple units and assets. The success of these operations suggests that mechanized maneuver is not yet obsolete, despite the challenges posed by modern battlefield conditions. However, carrying out such operations on a drone-saturated battlefield requires new strategies and tactics. Armored forces must continue to adapt to the changing nature of warfare, prioritizing stealth and agility over brute force in order to achieve success on the modern battlefield. The Army's continued investment in armor reflects its recognition of the enduring importance of these vehicles on the battlefield. Capt. Kevin Rincon, troop commander of the multifunctional reconnaissance company, emphasized that armor will remain a vital component of military operations. This perspective is underscored by the recent exercise at Hohenfels, where the rotating armored brigade was tasked with adapting to emerging threats and technologies. By leveraging drones, electronic warfare, and counter-drone systems, the 1/1 ABCT demonstrated its ability to sense, track, and engage attacks from an opposing force. The successful integration of these advanced technologies with traditional armor capabilities highlights the evolving nature of modern warfare. The exercise showcased how emerging technologies can facilitate combined arms maneuver, enabling forces to attack, seize, and retain terrain more effectively. However, this approach also presents challenges, particularly in countering enemies that possess significant overhead surveillance capabilities. To overcome these obstacles, military commanders must develop strategies for integrating advanced technologies with traditional armor tactics. This requires a nuanced understanding of the strengths and limitations of each component, as well as their potential synergies.
